Its uses include descriptions of territory, genealogical references, commands concerning the region, and statements about events associated with it. Gemalli is a personal name, not a common word describing an object, action, or quality. It identifies one individual in the Hebrew Old Testament and appears only once, in Numbers 13:12. English Bible renderings preserve it as “Gemalli,” treating it as a name rather than translating it into an ordinary meaning phrase. Its precise force in any verse depends on what is being trodden and the surrounding sentence.

e.t: This Hebrew noun refers to the young—people who are in the early stage of life. It normally functions as a designation for young people rather than as an action or quality. In the Old Testament, it occurs 46 times, showing that it is a regularly used word for this age group. Its surrounding setting may clarify whether the word points to young people generally or to a particular group of them. The central meaning remains “young.”
